stem: Select every capability explicitly listed as required for the lecture’s Turing-test discussion.

options.text: Computer vision for judging a participant’s physical appearance

citations.locator: Printed slide 8; The Turing Test; supporting panel(s): Turing-test component capabilities
citations.evidenceText: The Turing Test • A human judge converses (via text) with a human and a machine. If the judge cannot reliably tell which is which, the machine passes. • The Turing test was proposed by Alan Turing in 1950 in a paper titled "Computing Machinery and Intelligence." • Components required: – Natural Language Processing – Knowledge Representation – Automated Reasoning – Machine Learning • No machine has fully passed an unrestricted Turing Test. • CAPTCHA is an inverse Turing Test. 8

solution.justification: The list contains language processing, represented knowledge, reasoning and learning. A text-only interaction does not add a requirement for a hydraulic body.

optionExplanations.W01-L02-Q-010-o1: Correct: it is one of the four listed capabilities.
optionExplanations.W01-L02-Q-010-o5: This is not in the four-item list for the text-only test; it confuses additional embodied/visual capabilities with the stated test.

solution.simpleExplanation: Language, knowledge, reasoning and learning form the slide’s four-part list.
